rv.q: A surprisingly funny and relevant piece of work, three decades on.
The thirtieth anniversary production of Ayub Khan Din’s East Is East demonstrates the play retains the power to both shock and entertain.
This iteration needs a little more care in its construction to ensure the delivery is as punch-perfect as when it first took to the stage.
The sparky, sweary script is as laugh-out-loud funny as ever and well worth a revisit – even if Kash Arshad’s production struggles somewhat with the harsher aspects of the story.
It is a brilliantly funny production that manages to balance cracking humour without diminishing the serious issues raised.
This is a powerfully funny production with real dark moments, performed by a talented cast who each bring energy to their characters and build a world which the audience can truly invest in.
East is East is a hilarious and heartfelt production and is a joy to watch.
Bhasker Patel makes him sympathetic as well as comic, a trifle exaggerated at first (but that brings the laughs) – then movingly baffled as the whole tone of the play changes after the interval.

cn.t: Critics praise this timely 30th-anniversary revival of Ayub Khan Din's modern classic, celebrating its thoughtful blend of comedy and drama while exploring family, cultural identity, and integration in 1970s Britain with continued relevance today.
